goal: Migrate the Ledger Account Settlement slice to the shared Effect runtime and introduce service-layer idempotency for its mutating actions and nested Transaction creation.

tasks.name: Replace Transaction-only claims with a shared service
inputs: Effect runtime and shared error conventions
tasks.description: Add one Effect IdempotencyService used by domain services. Scope claims by Organization, action, and the unchanged client key; nested mutating service calls acquire distinct action-scoped claims with that same client key. Store only the completed resource ID and let the caller reload its source entity on replay. Keep header validation and forwarding in routes, with claim ownership in services.

tests: A completed claim contains only its resource ID
The same client key is independent across actions
Replay reloads the resource through the calling service
acceptance: No Transaction-specific idempotency service remains
Idempotency is acquired by services rather than HTTP middleware
Nested Settlement posting and Transaction creation both acquire claims

tasks.name: Add the local Settlement schema and entity
tasks.description: Create exact local TypeBox contracts and a relocated Settlement entity. Use the shared Metadata type, Luxon DateTime, Effect-based request and row decoding, parseId, and schema-owned Drizzle insert type. The entity owns lifecycle transition validation and conversion to a balanced Posted LedgerTransaction entity. Do not add clone helpers for repository-owned amount or Transaction-link updates.

tests: Local request and response schemas retain the current fields, required properties, patterns, defaults, descriptions, and OpenAPI IDs
toResponse omits externalReference and effectiveAtUpperBound and returns an empty string when no Transaction is linked
Request conversion creates a fresh ID and timestamps or reuses the supplied Settlement ID while replacing Created and Updated Time
Row conversion and serialization preserve metadata, null handling, TypeIDs, and dates
transitionTo accepts every valid lifecycle edge and rejects invalid edges
toTransaction returns a balanced Posted LedgerTransaction entity with the correct directions and metadata precedence
acceptance: The Settlement schema imports no legacy Ledger route schema
The entity performs no I/O and preserves every baseline conversion behavior
Focused entity tests pass

tasks.name: Add the Effect Drizzle repository
inputs: Current promise Settlement repository and tests
Unchanged Settlement and Settlement Entry tables
tasks.description: Add an Effect repository interface, Context.Service tag, live implementation, and Layer alongside the legacy repository. Translate only the current foreign-key and no-self-settlement failures into the existing errors. Preserve sequential Entry validation, check-then-insert exclusivity, onConflictDoNothing, Organization and Ledger predicates, descending Created Time ordering without a tie-breaker, drafting-only full updates and deletes, Updated Time writes, and the absence of transaction wrappers.

tests: Port every existing repository assertion to a managed PostgreSQL Layer

Cover list pagination and ordering, Organization isolation, ignored Ledger scope on item methods, constraint errors, drafting-only writes, Entry eligibility and exclusivity, amount calculation, and status updates
effectiveAtUpperBound round-trips through storage without gathering Entries
A Pending-to-Drafting status update retains linked Entries
acceptance: Repository methods return Effects and use DatabaseTag.effectDb
No schema, migration, transaction, lock, retry, index, or uniqueness change appears
Focused repository tests pass against PostgreSQL

tasks.name: Add the Effect Settlement service
inputs: Current promise Settlement service and tests
Approved Settlement lifecycle and posting behavior
tasks.description: Add the Effect Settlement service, Context.Service tag, and Layer. Move Ledger and Account orchestration from routes into the service. Every mutating Settlement action acquires its own action-scoped idempotency claim. Posting asks the entity for a LedgerTransaction and calls TransactionService with the same client key, producing a second Transaction-scoped claim. Use focused repository operations for calculated amount and Transaction linkage; lifecycle validation remains on the entity.

tests: Port existing service coverage to complete repository, Ledger, Account, and Transaction mock Layers
List performs the Ledger check before the repository query
Create and update use the settled Account's currency and Normal Balance and reject mismatched currencies with the existing conflict
Update validates Accounts before loading the Settlement and persists an entity with replaced Created Time
Every lifecycle edge and invalid transition remains unchanged
processing to pending attempts the drafting-only full update and skips the status update when that write fails
pending to posted creates the Posted Transaction before linking it and skips the final status write when linking fails
Posting preserves the client idempotency key across distinct Settlement and Transaction action claims, Entry directions, description fallback, and Settlement metadata precedence
pending to drafting performs only the existing status update and does not release Entries
Transaction creation failure or a non-Posted result prevents linking and status mutation
acceptance: All service methods return Effects
The service depends directly on existing Effect services without a promise bridge
No transaction wrapper, clock policy, or concurrency policy beyond the approved concurrent Account lookups is introduced
Focused service tests pass

tasks.name: Compose Settlement into the managed runtime
inputs: Existing Ledger, Account, Transaction, database, and runtime services
tasks.description: Export one Settlement Layer and add it to the server runtime. Supply it with the existing database, Ledger, Account, Transaction, and shared Idempotency Layers. Do not create another runtime, database client, executor, lifecycle hook, or Settlement-specific override.

tests: Resolve the Settlement service from the default server runtime
Build the API package with the production runtime composition
acceptance: ServerRuntimeServices includes the Settlement service
The runtime supplies the Settlement service's Ledger, Account, Transaction, repository, and database dependencies
Layer composition reuses the existing database, service Layers, and runtime disposal
The API package typecheck and build pass without production composition casts

tasks.name: Move routes and route tests to the Effect service
inputs: Current Settlement routes, tests, and response snapshots
Organization and Transaction route execution patterns
tasks.description: Relocate all eight handlers and switch the Ledger router to the new slice. Preserve route paths, permissions, status codes, and response serialization. Require and forward the shared Idempotency-Key header on every mutating action while leaving claim handling in the service. Each handler executes one Settlement program through the managed runtime.

tests: Retain route coverage for all eight operations, pagination, validation, permissions, success bodies, and typed failures
Create, delete, Entry mutation, and transitions still return HTTP 200
Get, delete, Entry mutation, and applicable transitions accept a different valid Ledger path without passing that Ledger to the service
List passes the Ledger and pagination values
Responses retain the current omissions and empty Transaction ID fallback
Unexpected service failures become the current generic HTTP 500 response
Existing response snapshots remain unchanged after relocation
acceptance: Every handler runs one Effect program through request.server.runtime
Successful entities are converted with toResponse and typed failures are rethrown unchanged
The public HTTP and OpenAPI contracts are unchanged
Focused route tests pass

tasks.name: Remove legacy wiring and run regression validation
inputs: All legacy Settlement imports and Fastify decorations
Repository validation commands from AGENTS.md and the approved design
tasks.description: Delete the promise Settlement implementation and Transaction bridge. Remove only Settlement ownership from the legacy repository and service plugins, shared route schema, shared fixtures, and entity exports. Keep those plugins and fixtures intact for Categories, Statements, and Balance Monitors. Review the final diff for any behavior, schema, dependency, or infrastructure change outside the approved migration.

acceptance: No legacy Settlement repository, service decoration, promise bridge, or old Settlement schema import remains
Categories, Statements, and Balance Monitors retain their existing plugin and fixture wiring

The final diff contains no database migration, schema snapshot change, dependency update, transaction wrapper, concurrency policy beyond the approved concurrent Account lookups, or unrelated cleanup beyond the approved shared idempotency capability
